title: Coding agents and maintainers surfaced different types of software defects
summary: Across 20 open-source repositories, arithmetic and comparison errors made up 18.5% of agent reports and 9.9% of historical maintainer fixes. Missing branches for supported inputs made up 7.7% of agent reports and 18.0% of the fixes. The study compared 14 agent configurations with 2,457 fixes from 18 months of repository history.
ai_technology: Frontier coding agents including GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash

source_review.scope: §§2–4, Table 4 and taxonomy Appendix D aggregate methods

evidence.tested: The study categorized agent reports from historical snapshots and same-repository fixes using a shared bug taxonomy. Agent percentages were averages across configurations.
evidence.unknown: The comparison contrasts reported findings with fixes that maintainers chose to complete. Some reports may be invalid, and unreported or unfixed historical bugs are outside the reference set.
evidence.ai_role: Coding agents generated bug reports for historical snapshots. Additional learned classification and matching helped construct and categorize the analysis set.
